market_wrap.text: Nifty rose 1.12% to 25,801 and the Sensex gained about 898 points for a second straight up day, led by private and PSU banks as foreign funds turned buyers; India held up while Asian markets slumped on a global sell-off in AI stocks, helped by softer crude. Breadth was weak, though: the Nifty Smallcap 100 slipped 0.13%. Your stocks and ETFs fell 2.7% (about ₹2,541) because gold and silver crashed again on US rate-hike bets; mutual-fund NAVs for today are not out yet, so fund values are unchanged.

reasons.reason: Gold and silver slumped again as a near-19-month high in the dollar, elevated US bond yields and about a 97% market-implied chance of a December Fed rate rise hit bullion; MCX silver fell about 6% and gold about 4% in early trade. Silver ETFs were down as much as 7.5% in the morning before recovering part of the fall.
No company news found today. Netweb, an AI-server maker, slipped as AI hardware stocks sold off across Asia (Taiwan's index fell 6.2% and Korea's over 5%), even though Indian IT services stocks rose.

Today was the last day of Indo Borax's open offer for Kronox shares at ₹157.27, well below the market price, and a filing disclosed that Indo Borax has now pledged its entire 64.26% stake to lenders for the acquisition loan. No other company news found today.
No company news found today. Small caps lagged the large-cap rally (Nifty Smallcap 100 down 0.13%), and KRN gave back part of Thursday's gain.

news.headline: Promoter's entire 64.26% Kronox stake now pledged
news.summary: Indo Borax disclosed a further pledge of 50.26% of Kronox's shares (created 17 November), so all of its 64.26% holding now secures the roughly ₹225 crore loan used to buy the stake. The ₹157.27 open offer closed today.

news.headline: Gold heads for biggest weekly fall since March; silver at lowest since Sep 2025
news.summary: MCX gold has fallen about 9% in three sessions and silver about 13%, as Fed officials signal further rate rises, US 10-year yields stay above 5% and the dollar strengthens.

events.detail: Shareholders vote on the new Chairman (Mudit Kumar Singh) and Managing Director (Deep Saraf); the e-voting cut-off date is 20 November.
Meeting runs 2–4 December. The RBI raised rates in October; another rise would weigh on your bond fund and on small and mid caps.
Meeting runs 8–9 December; markets expect a rate rise, the main pressure on silver and gold lately.
events.affects: Silver and gold funds (about 30% of the portfolio)

events.detail: Companies usually report from mid-January to mid-February; results moved Manorama, Hindustan Copper and KRN this quarter.

outlook.view: Gold fell below $3,800 to a 14-month low and silver lost about 3% as markets put roughly 96% odds on a December US rate rise; the Silver Institute still projects a sixth straight annual supply deficit.
outlook.watch: The 8–9 December US Fed decision (about 90% priced for a hike) and the dollar.

outlook.view: They led today and have outperformed large caps this year, but they fall harder when rates rise or foreign investors sell.
outlook.watch: RBI decision on 4 December and foreign investor flows.

outlook.view: AI demand is lifting hardware makers like Netweb, but a global sell-off in AI stocks hit Indian IT today (Nifty IT −0.9%).
Record copper prices drove Hindustan Copper's profit surge, but copper has since slipped to a five-month low on a strong dollar and weak China data, dragging metal stocks.
outlook.watch: Global copper prices and the dollar.

outlook.view: The RBI is in a tightening phase, which tends to lower bond prices in the short term and raise yields on new bonds.
